A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GraphPFN and contain readable main text, figures, tables and Appendices A–D. All 16 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2 were inspected, and relocated material could be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original GraphPFN benchmark results in Tables 2–3, pretraining curves in Figure 2 and an adapter-pretraining ablation in Table 4.

after.justification: v2 reports revised benchmark results, numerical analyses of synthetic and real graphs, generator comparisons and an adapter-pretraining ablation in Tables 1–6.

M1.justification: The backbone, graph adapters and combined graph prior remain, but the reported procedure introduces two-stage pretraining, weight averaging, eight random input features and prediction ensembling. Section 3.2 also replaces the blanket cross-entropy objective description with cross-entropy for classification and mean squared error for regression. These substantially revise reported training and inference.

E1.justification: The same 13 downstream datasets and node-level classification/regression tasks remain, as confirmed by v1 Table 1 and v2 Table 7. Synthetic training coverage expands within the new controls: Appendix B.3 trains models on Erdős–Rényi, standalone degree-corrected SBM and preferential-attachment graph distributions instead of the combined prior.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated OpenGraph, AnyGraph, TS-GNN, GCOPE and TAG comparisons on classification datasets, while removing G2T-TabPFNv2 rows from both benchmark tables. G2T-LimiX and the traditional baselines remain. TAG matches the earlier-cited TabGFM, but its evaluation is new; TAG-TabPFNv2 is distinct from the removed G2T-TabPFNv2 comparator.

E3.justification: Pretraining changes from 500,000 steps using four million graphs to 10,000 plus 4,000 optimizer steps using 2.24 million graphs, with gradient accumulation, larger second-stage graphs and AdamW/cosine scheduling replacing Adam/constant learning rate. Evaluation adds ensemble-based validation/testing and average ranks. New analyses sample 1,000 graphs and compare generators using only stage one. Downstream splits and task metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.2–B.3 quantitatively compares synthetic and real graph characteristics and tests the proposed generator against three simpler alternatives. The retained adapter-pretraining ablation changes from nine mixed benchmarks to eight GraphLand datasets, adding three GraphLand cases and removing four classic cases. The explicit with/without-LapPE comparisons disappear.

E5.justification: Both versions retain ten evaluation runs and mean±standard-deviation reporting. v2 newly specifies ten different seeds per prediction ensemble and reports distribution summaries, including quartiles, for sampled synthetic graphs. Its new generator-ablation Table 5 provides point scores without uncertainty values. No increase in independent repeated evaluation runs is stated.

E6.justification: Many results are replaced under revised settings: GraphPFN FT on artnet-exp changes from 53.08±0.23 to 50.64±1.27, while twitch-views changes from OOM to 78.17±0.13. v2 adds ensemble, graph-characteristics and generator-ablation results and revises adapter-ablation scores. Appendix D explains that pubmed entries in FT rows reuse ICL results; they do not demonstrate successful finetuning.

T1.justification: The graph-construction mathematics and SCM formulation remain substantively unchanged. v2 explains standard cumulative-degree and regression statistics for empirical analysis but adds no substantive theoretical definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction remove the stated 50,000-node qualification and narrow the novelty wording to the first publicly available PFN designed and pretrained specifically for graph node-level tasks. The central contributions—a synthetic graph prior, graph-aware PFN and strong downstream performance—remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds an interpretation of the second training stage as essential and connects the road-network ablation exception to the prior's community/core-periphery bias. It removes the earlier hm-prices edge-count mismatch explanation and explicit limited-ablation caveat. The broader pretraining explanation and memory, class-count and node-task limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies SCM GNN choices, LapPE probability and dimensions, endpoint-embedding multiplication for the MGM head, accumulation and weight-averaging parameters, and detailed ensemble/shuffling/early-stopping procedures. Appendix D discloses the pubmed ICL fallback. Conversely, the graph-tool implementation and generation-speed disclosure disappear. The code-access statement is retained.

R1.justification: v2 emphasizes graph-specific pretraining relative to tabularization approaches and adds references including TabPFN-GN, TabPFN-2.5, TabICLv2 and work on random features and graph statistics. The overall PFN/GFM positioning remains. TabGFM becoming TAG and several publication updates concern retained works rather than new research additions.

P1.justification: The abstract and much of the introduction are substantially rewritten, and the results narrative is reorganized around three observations instead of two. Pretraining exposition is restructured, while the appendices reorganize graph examples and analyses ahead of the adapter comparison. These changes extend beyond local wording corrections.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, and Figure 2 expands from four to eight panels with revised axes and a training-stage divider. Main tables gain reorganized rows/columns, average ranks and expanded captions. Three prior-analysis tables are added, dataset statistics move to the appendix, and two graph-example figures are replaced by one six-graph figure.

improvement.justification: v1 supported its central graph-prior design largely through motivation, visual examples and an adapter-pretraining comparison. v2 adds generator comparisons using the same first-stage budget and quantitative synthetic/real graph analyses, substantially strengthening that evidence, alongside broader baseline comparisons and clearer reproducibility details. These gains outweigh the removed LapPE and classic-dataset adapter analyses. Limitations remain: generator comparisons lack uncertainty values, and pubmed ICL substitutions in FT rows are explained only in Appendix D.
